intro: Bahrain is an island kingdom that was once the centre of the ancient Dilmun civilisation and later the first Gulf state to find oil.

chapters.title: Dilmun
text: Around 4,000 years ago Bahrain was the heart of Dilmun, a trading power between Mesopotamia and the Indus valley. Mesopotamian stories called it a paradise. Tens of thousands of burial mounds from that time still dot the island.
Bahrain's fresh-water springs and pearls made it valuable for thousands of years.

chapters.title: Rulers and Britain
text: Persians and Portuguese held Bahrain at times. The Al Khalifa family, who still rule, took control in 1783. Britain signed treaties with Bahrain in the 1800s and protected it.

chapters.title: Oil and independence
text: In 1932 Bahrain became the first place on the Arab side of the Gulf to strike oil. It became independent in 1971 and a kingdom in 2002. In 2011 large protests, many led by the Shia majority, were put down with help from Saudi forces.

timeline.title: Oil
timeline.text: The first oil strike in the Arab Gulf.
